description: Gradient decomposition of dt_emb parameter across conditions. Measures L2 norm of gradient from each loss component (obs decoder, reward, KL, cont) w.r.t. dt_embedding.weight. 50 batches of 16x64 sequences each, seed=42.
methodology: For each batch: forward pass through world model, compute individual losses (obs/reward/KL/cont), backward each separately, record gradient L2 norm on dt_emb. Percentages = component_norm / sum_of_all_norms.

steps.config: Full-SGS model, measured WITHOUT SGS to show underlying gradient structure
steps.note: With SGS active during training: obs=0%, reward=0%, kl=100%, cont=0% (all head gradients blocked from dt_emb)

key_findings.without_sgs: Obs decoder gradients account for 32-40% of total gradient on dt_emb across all conditions, confirming that observation reconstruction is a major gradient driver for the temporal embedding.
key_findings.with_sgs: Full-SGS blocks all head loss gradients (obs+reward+cont) from reaching dt_emb, leaving only KL (100%). This is the mechanism that prevents CIVO.
key_findings.contrast: The gradient structure is roughly balanced (obs ~35-40%, reward ~25-36%, kl ~26-35%) without SGS. SGS eliminates the obs and reward pathways entirely.

prior_analysis_comparison.note: Earlier analysis (in gen_figures.py) reported 008d at 55K: obs=25.8%, reward=23.5%, KL=50.7%, and at 105K: obs=93%, reward=0%, KL=7%. The discrepancy likely reflects different batch sampling or accumulated training gradients vs. per-batch counterfactual measurement. The qualitative conclusion (obs is a significant gradient source) is consistent.
